name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator
one_sentence_pitch: The BRE flight program seeks to establish the burning conditions in a quiescent microgravity ambient in terms of material properties.
plain_summary: The BRE flight program seeks to establish the burning conditions in a quiescent microgravity ambient in terms of material properties. The specific flight objectives are as follows. 1. Observe burning behavior in long-duration microgravity for CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2mixtures on porous circular burners of 25 and 50 mm diameter.
objectives: The BRE flight program seeks to establish the burning conditions in a quiescent microgravity ambient in terms of material properties.
The specific flight objectives are as follows. 1.
Observe burning behavior in long-duration microgravity for CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2mixtures on porous circular burners of 25 and 50 mm diameter.
Consider O2/N2 ambients with various pressures and ambient O2 concentrations and pressures.
method: To accomplish the above objectives, flight experiments are proposed. Additionally, preliminary flight tests will be performed to verify the experiment operations and for comparison with ground-based tests. For each test, conditions will be established for the chamber contents, namely choice of diluent, oxygen concentration, and pressure.
main_findings: BRE yielded important data relevant to spacecraft fire safety.

Quasi-steady burning corresponding to various condensed-phase materials (such as PMMA and Nylon) was observed in microgravity despite the absence of air flow, where the cessation of ventilation is an established step in putting out spacecraft fires.

The ongoing combustion without air flow was notably seen in elevated-oxygen atmospheres which are being considered for use in future spacecraft, whereas such flames in a normal atmosphere of 21% oxygen self-extinguished in a short time.

While BRE’s results are still preliminary, they suggest that NASA may want to increase use of its alternative flammability Test 2, with the cone calorimeter, where that test can measure material properties corresponding to the microgravity flames observed with the BRE burner.
safety_relevance: Supports NASA’s prevention pillar of spacecraft fire safety.
